name: application-speaker-card
title: Speaker Card
description: Conference speaker card with an initials avatar, name, title/company, a quoted talk title, and a row of social link icons.
useWhen: A conference or event site needs a speaker grid or lineup listing presenters and their talks.
You want the talk title visually distinguished from the speaker's own bio/title line.
Social links (X, LinkedIn, personal site) should be reachable without cluttering the main text.
avoidWhen: The person isn't giving a talk (no talk title to show) — use a plain profile or team-section card instead.
You need a photo, not initials — swap the avatar span for an while keeping the same layout.
There are many speakers needing dense list scanning rather than card browsing — use a table or compact list row instead.
responsiveBehavior: The card is a fixed max-w-xs block that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: Each social icon link has a specific aria-label naming both the platform and the speaker, not a generic 'link'.
The talk title is set apart with a background and quotation marks, visually and semantically distinct from the speaker's bio line.
Text content (name, title, talk) remains selectable and readable by screen readers; nothing critical is encoded only in the avatar.

variants.title: Speaker card
variants.description: Elena Lindqvist, Principal Engineer at Northwind Labs, with her talk title and X/LinkedIn/website social links.
accessibility: Social icons are aria-hidden with the accessible name carried by each link's aria-label instead.

variants.title: Speaker card (Dark)
variants.description: Speaker card adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Talk-title background and social icon colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
